payload.answer: Shouldn't only my intent recorded and commited? Meaning INT files? therefore we wouldn't need my words to be commiteed, correct?

options.description: Keeps today's behaviour since early October: each message a record comes from goes into git with it; messages that make no record stay private. The older choice is narrowed to say that.
options.label: Commit the whole message (Recommended)

options.description: Commit only the sentences a record quotes, not the whole message. The judge then sees less context in a fresh clone; the premise code and its tests change before landing.
options.label: Only the quoted sentences

options.description: No words of yours are committed; the judge reads them only from this machine's session log and a fresh clone can't judge. Needs a rewrite of the judge's input and tests.
options.label: Nothing of my words in git

payload.question: Correction to my last question. When a record comes from one of your messages, plumb commits that whole message (not just quoted sentences) to git with the record, so a fresh clone can judge it. Messages that produce no record stay private on this machine. An older choice says no message text goes into git at all. Which should hold?
